title: Configuring Production Kubernetes Ingress & Automated SSL/TLS with Cert-Manager and Let's Encrypt
summary: Step-by-step setup of Ingress-Nginx, automated zero-touch certificate issuance and renewals with Let's Encrypt ACME ClusterIssuers.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.article-objectives: Fully automate SSL/TLS certificate issuance, provisioning, and renewals for production Kubernetes clusters, eliminating the risk of operational downtime from expired certificates.
sections.architecture-principles:
Ingress security architecture:

  • Ingress-Nginx Controller: Edge proxy routing external HTTP/HTTPS traffic to internal Kubernetes Services.
  • Cert-Manager Operator: Kubernetes Custom Controller monitoring Certificate CRDs and solving Let's Encrypt ACME HTTP-01/DNS-01 challenges.
  • Kubernetes Secrets: Storing TLS keypairs (tls.crt, tls.key) mounted into Ingress resources.
sections.step-by-step-setup:
Implementation roadmap:

  • Step 1: Deploy Cert-Manager via official Helm charts with installCRDs=true.
  • Step 2: Configure production ClusterIssuer pointing to Let's Encrypt ACME v2 endpoints.
  • Step 3: Annotate Ingress manifests with cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod.
sections.troubleshooting-pitfalls:
• HTTP-01 Challenge Failed: Cloud Security Groups blocking inbound port 80 (Let's Encrypt requires port 80 for domain validation).
  • Let's Encrypt Rate Limits: Always validate configurations against Let's Encrypt Staging issuers first.
sections.evaluation-scaling: Automated SSL certificate renewals across 50+ enterprise subdomains 30 days prior to expiration with zero human intervention.

title: Crafting Clean Code: Eliminating God Objects and Refactoring Anemic Domain Models
summary: Strategies for decomposing bloated multi-thousand line classes into cohesive Aggregate Roots adhering to Clean Code and Object-Oriented principles.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.problem-statement: In legacy codebases, service classes like OrderService frequently explode beyond 3,000 lines with dozens of dependencies. Entities degenerate into dumb data bags with public getters/setters (Anemic Domain Model), scattering critical business logic throughout the application.
sections.initial-approach: Developers often append more conditional if/else branches or create static utility classes, worsening coupling and violating the Single Responsibility Principle.
sections.optimization-thinking:
Transition to a Rich Domain Model:

  • Encapsulate domain validations and state transitions directly within Entities.
  • Eliminate public setters and enforce invariant constraints upon entity creation.
  • Employ Domain Events for cross-aggregate communication instead of direct service coupling.
sections.code-implementation:
Refactoring domain logic into encapsulated entities:

public class Order {
  private OrderStatus status;
  private List items;

  public void applyDiscount(DiscountCode code) {
    if (this.status != OrderStatus.DRAFT) {
      throw new IllegalStateException("Cannot discount confirmed order");
    }
    // Encapsulated domain logic
  }
}
sections.complexity-applications: Decreased Cyclomatic Complexity by 60%, boosted unit test coverage beyond 85%, and allowed new engineering team members to comprehend domain rules intuitively.

title: Backend Architecture Evolution: From Monolith to Microservices and the Rise of Modular Monolith
summary: A 10-year retrospective on architectural trends, evaluating the hidden operational costs of microservices and why Modular Monoliths represent the pragmatic choice for modern engineering teams.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.introduction: The rush to adopt Microservices dominated the past decade. By 2026, leading engineering organizations are pragmatically consolidating systems into Modular Monoliths to reduce distributed network friction and cloud operational overhead.
sections.multi-dimensional-evaluation:
Comparative analysis of architectural paradigms:

  • Traditional Monolith: Simple deployment, but risks becoming an unmaintainable Big Ball of Mud without strict code boundaries.
  • Microservices: Autonomous team deployments, yet incurs high network latency, distributed transaction complexity (Sagas), and observability friction.
  • Modular Monolith: Strict Bounded Context boundaries within a single deployable artifact. Leverages ultra-fast in-memory calls with seamless readiness for future microservice extraction.
sections.case-study-experience: Consolidated 6 fragmented microservices into a unified Go Modular Monolith. AWS infrastructure costs dropped 65%, inter-service gRPC timeouts disappeared, and feature development throughput doubled.
sections.actionable-recommendations: Start with a well-bounded Modular Monolith. Only decompose into Microservices when independent hardware scaling or organizational boundaries (>50 engineers) truly necessitate it.
sections.open-questions-discussion: Has your engineering team experienced 'Microservices Fatigue'? What architectural boundaries have worked best in your domain?

title: Applying Domain-Driven Design (DDD) & Hexagonal Architecture in Golang Microservices
summary: Structuring Go services with Ports & Adapters to decouple core domain business rules from external frameworks, SQL drivers, and transport protocols.
author: Huỳnh Nhật Tân

sections.context-problem: In naive Golang projects, SQL queries and HTTP JSON parsing often intermingle inside handlers. Swapping databases or adding gRPC interfaces forces intrusive rewrites across business logic.
sections.system-requirements:
• Technology Independence: Core domain rules must remain free from external libraries and database drivers.
  • Testability: 100% unit test coverage for use cases using mock interfaces without live database connections.
sections.architecture-design:
Ports & Adapters (Hexagonal Architecture) structure:

  • Domain Core: Pure entities and domain services importing standard Go libraries only.
  • Ports: Contracts defined as Go interfaces (e.g. UserRepository, PaymentGateway).
  • Adapters: Concrete implementations (HTTP Handlers, gRPC Servers, PostgreSQL Repositories, Redis Caches).
sections.trade-offs-analysis:
Initial boilerplate vs long-term maintainability:

  • Hexagonal architecture requires additional interface declarations and data transfer mappings up front.
  • In exchange, long-term maintenance costs drop by 50% as underlying database drivers and cloud infrastructure evolve.
sections.lessons-best-practices: Define Port interfaces in the consumer package (Consumer Interface pattern in Go) rather than bundling them alongside the adapter implementations.
